name: Melissa A. Long
description: Concurred, argued that Mr. Brown had a reasonable expectation of privacy in his conversation with his mother, and the police violated his Fourth Amendment and state constitutional rights by recording it.

name: Justice Goldberg
description: Concurred, argued that the plaintiffs lacked standing to challenge the Reproductive Privacy Act and that the General Assembly had the constitutional authority to enact it.

name: Robinson, J.
description: Concurred in part and dissented in part, argued that the court should only rule on the issue of standing and not address other substantive issues.

name: Justice Lynch Prata
description: Did not participate in the decision.

name: Justice Long
description: Did not participate in the decision.

name: Justice Lynch Prata
description: Concurred, argued that the civil death statute is unconstitutional because it completely deprives life-sentenced prisoners of their right to bring civil actions, violating Article 1, Section 5 of the Rhode Island Constitution.

name: Justice Goldberg
description: Dissented, argued that the civil death statute should be addressed prospectively by the General Assembly, not the court, and that the majority's decision will unnecessarily open floodgates to frivolous inmate claims.

name: Chief Justice Suttell
description: Concurred, argued that the plaintiff's claims under RICRA were precluded by prior federal Title IX decisions and that the Rhode Island Constitution's antidiscrimination clause does not create a private right of action.

name: Justice Long
description: Did not participate in the decision.
